Anya: Quick design review for the 'Cost Lens' layout — proposing a compact mode that collapses per-model token breakdown into expandable rows. Need feedback on: org vs project toggle placement, invoice download discoverability, token-unit labeling, and a11y for keyboard/screen-reader. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (compact-mode frames at page 'Cost Lens / Compact'). Sam: Saw the frames — nice direction. Key asks: keep total spend + the org/project toggle pinned at top, move invoice download into the right-hand header as a dropdown, and add a lightweight `token units` legend under the chart. GIF preview attached in figma. :eyes: Maria: Implementation concern — expanding rows for large orgs could create hundreds of DOM nodes and tank client performance. Suggest virtualization for the list and server-side aggregates for collapsed state. Also we should emit telemetry for expand/collapse to see real usage. Kevin: A11y nits already: the new gradient on spend bars fails WCAG AA at 14px for the numeric labels. Options: use a solid fill with higher contrast, add patterned fills, or increase label weight/size. Keyboard: when toggling org/project, focus should remain on the toggle control, not jump. Screen reader: chart needs an accessible description. Example hidden text: `span.sr-only "Spending chart for {orgName}, showing total spend and per-project breakdown"`. Anya: Good catches. @ops-bot can you queue an a11y scan on the compact frames? Also we should prototype the keyboard walkthrough (tab order + arrow key nav for rows). ops-bot: a11y-checker queued: running on branch `feature/cost-lens-compact`. Preliminary results: 5 contrast issues, 2 missing ARIA attributes, animations flagged for >2s. Full report URL: https://ci.redwood.ai/a11y/582/report Sam: Copy thought: current button reads `Download invoice`. Should we be explicit about formats? Options: `Download invoice (CSV)`, `Download (CSV & PDF)`, or a single `Download` with a caret for format choices. I slightly prefer dropdown to avoid clutter. Maria: Backend note — CSV export is cheap, PDF needs a renderer (we have a service for that but it adds latency). Technically fine to offer both; suggest providing a single `Download` that opens a small menu with `CSV` and `PDF` so we only call PDF renderer on explicit selection. Anya: Decision lean: dropdown with default `CSV`, menu option for `PDF`. Tooltip on the button: `Download invoice for selected org/project and date range`. Also add a tooltip next to `tokens` label: `What are token units?` linking to docs. Kevin: For screen readers, we should also add `aria-live="polite"` region for chart updates and use `role="table"`+`aria-label` on the expanded rows so AT users can navigate. Sample snippet: ```html
...
``` Sam: I'll update Figma — adding high-contrast palette options, explicit focus outlines, and the dropdown for invoice formats. Will also add a compact-mode microinteraction GIF showing keyboard nav. Expect updated frames in ~10m. Maria: I'll spike virtualization and aggregated-rows API; will measure client memory and render times. Aiming to have numbers by EOD tomorrow. Anya: Action checklist (quick): 1) Dropdown for invoice formats (UX + backend) 2) Keyboard walkthrough + a11y test cases 3) Perf spike (virtualization + aggregated rows) 4) Tooltips / copy tweaks / tokens explainer. @Maria you own #3, @Kevin own #2, @Sam design updates. Maria: Yep, owning #3. Kevin: Owning #2 — will write test cases and a small keyboard demo harness. Sam: Posting updated frames now. deploy-bot: Staging build created for `feature/cost-lens-compact` (build #582) — preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/582 Anya: Thanks everyone — sync in tomorrow's product standup if anything blocks. :raised_hands:
